title: Jacobian presentation of completed Kähler differentials
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $S$ a finitely generated $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], $\mathfrak p\subset S$ a maximal ideal, $A=S_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $F=S/\mathfrak p$, and let $\widehat A$ be the maximal-ideal completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Assume $F/k$ is finite separable [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension] and fix a $k$-algebra section $\sigma:F\to\widehat A$ of the residue map; let $F$ act on $\widehat A$ through $\sigma$. Suppose a continuous surjection of $F$-algebras $F[[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]\twoheadrightarrow\widehat A$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] has kernel generated by $f_1,\ldots,f_s\in(t_1,\ldots,t_n)$. Let $d:A\to\Omega_{A/k}$ be the universal derivation and let $\widehat d:\widehat A\to\Omega_{A/k}\otimes_A\widehat A$ be its continuous extension, characterized by $\widehat d\circ\sigma=0$ and compatibility with $d$ on $A$. Then the $\widehat A$-linear map from the cokernel of the Jacobian matrix $(\partial f_j/\partial t_i):\widehat A^{\oplus s}\to\widehat A^{\oplus n}$ to $\Omega_{A/k}\otimes_A\widehat A$ that sends the class of the $i$-th basis vector $e_i$ to $\widehat d(t_i)$ is an isomorphism, where $\Omega_{A/k}$ denotes Kähler differentials [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] and tensor products use [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product].

source.place: Tag 0C4D (lemma-nodal), polynomial Jacobian presentation in the algebraically closed proof paragraph; auxiliary completed-presentation comparison extending that argument via continuous differentials, with the finite-separable k-algebra coefficient section of Varieties Tag 0C52 (lemma-complete-local-ring-structure-as-algebra). The completed comparison is not a separate assertion of 0C4D.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-completion-kahler-differential-comparison](i) the universal derivation $d$ has a unique continuous extension $\widehat d:\widehat A\to\Omega_{A/k}\otimes_A\widehat A$. The composite $\widehat d\circ\sigma:F\to\Omega_{A/k}\otimes_A\widehat A$ is a $k$-derivation (σ is a $k$-algebra map and the target is an $F$-module through σ), so by the universal property of $\Omega_{F/k}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] it factors through $\Omega_{F/k}$, which is $0$ by [lem-trf-separable-field-differentials-vanish]. Hence $\widehat d\circ\sigma=0$, and the map $\widehat d$ of the statement exists and is the continuous extension of (i).

source.place: Tag 0C4D, algebraically closed Jacobian paragraph, with finite-separable coefficient-field descent and More Algebra Tag 0C34.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-completion-kahler-differential-comparison](ii) there is an $\widehat A$-linear isomorphism $\Phi:\Omega_{A/k}\otimes_A\widehat A\to\widehat\Omega_{\widehat A/F}$ onto the module of continuous $F$-differentials (defined there as $\varprojlim_r\Omega_{(\widehat A/\mathfrak m^r\widehat A)/F}$, $F$ acting through $\sigma$), with $\Phi(\widehat d(x))=\widehat{\mathrm d}_F(x)$ for all $x\in\widehat A$, in particular for the images of the $t_i$.

source.place: Tag 0C4D, passage from the local algebra to its completed power-series presentation.

proof.text: Let $\pi:D=F[[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]\to\widehat A$ be the given surjection, so $\widehat A\cong R=D/(f_1,\ldots,f_s)$ as $F$-algebras. The ideal $\pi(\mathfrak n)$, $\mathfrak n=(t_1,\ldots,t_n)$, is $\mathfrak m\widehat A$: by continuity each $\pi(t_i)$ is topologically nilpotent, hence lies in the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\widehat A$, and $\widehat A/\pi(\mathfrak n)$ is a nonzero quotient of $D/\mathfrak n=F$, hence equals $F=\widehat A/\mathfrak m\widehat A$ (elementary). So the two inverse systems defining continuous $F$-differentials agree, and [lem-trf-formal-power-series-continuous-differentials] gives an isomorphism $\Psi$ from the cokernel of the Jacobian map $\widehat A^{\oplus s}\to\widehat A^{\oplus n}$ to $\widehat\Omega_{\widehat A/F}$ with $\Psi(e_i)=\widehat{\mathrm d}_F(t_i)$.

source.place: Tag 0C4D, polynomial Jacobian presentation in the algebraically closed proof paragraph, extended to the completed coefficient-field presentation.

proof.text: The composite $\Phi^{-1}\circ\Psi$ is an $\widehat A$-linear isomorphism from the Jacobian cokernel to $\Omega_{A/k}\otimes_A\widehat A$, and by Steps 2 and 3 it sends the class of $e_i$ to $\Phi^{-1}(\widehat{\mathrm d}_F(t_i))=\widehat d(t_i)$. It is therefore the map of the statement, which is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0C4D, conclusion of the Jacobian presentation paragraph.
